editorial:
Imagine you are walking through the dark, dirty tunnels under London and realize you are not alone. That is exactly the kind of creepy feeling you get here. The story starts when a government guy goes missing, and the police finally start caring because too many people have vanished in the same spot. You also get to follow a couple who accidentally find a body, which kicks off a scary game of cat and mouse. The vibe is gritty and damp, making you feel like something is always lurking just around the corner in the shadows of the subway.

What really works is how the movie builds tension without needing a huge budget. The acting is solid, and the twist at the end is a total surprise that you won't see coming. While some parts move a bit slow, the payoff is worth it. If you love old-school scares, you should definitely track this down. It is a great pick for a rainy Friday night with the lights off.
endingExplained: You find out the killer is actually a man who was thought to be dead for years. He has been living in the tunnels and killing people to survive. In the final showdown, the police corner him in his underground lair. He tries to fight back, but he eventually falls to his death in the dark pits of the tunnels. The movie ends with the mystery solved and the tunnels finally becoming safe again.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves 70s horror and urban mysteries.
